title: AWS CWI Training in Corpus Christi, TX: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Corpus Christi refinery, LNG, export pipeline and offshore yard welders: corporate, online or one-to-one formats.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Corpus Christi: Six Days for Refinery, LNG, Pipeline and Yard Welding Inspectors
html:
Corpus Christi's welders work on the infrastructure that sends American energy overseas. The port bills itself as the country's number one crude oil export gateway, a liquefaction terminal across the bay in San Patricio County has just become the second-largest LNG facility in the United States, refineries line the Inner Harbor, and yards on the ship channel have built some of the biggest offshore topsides in the Gulf. Almost every one of those assets is a welded pressure boundary or structure that an inspector has to accept. Atlantis NDT runs a six-day (6-day) course preparing Coastal Bend welders, pipefitters, QC technicians and engineers for the American Welding Society's Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination. It is offered three ways: corporate delivery at an employer's facility, online study at your own pace with an instructor answering questions, and one-to-one sessions online or in person. AWS administers the examination and grants the certification to those who pass; Atlantis prepares people for it and certifies nobody. There is no Atlantis classroom in Corpus Christi, and AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed the course. To start, send a Corpus Christi CWI exam prep enquiry.

How the six-day course works for Coastal Bend candidates

The outline tracks the exam. Two days go to Part A Fundamentals, covering welding and cutting processes, AWS terminology and symbols, joint design, metallurgy, mechanical testing, NDT methods, discontinuities, safety and inspection math. Day three prepares for the Part B practical: gauges, weld measurement and applying procedure and qualification records. Day four works inside your Part C code book. Day five is timed practice papers, and day six closes gaps and covers exam logistics. The detailed daily plan is on the AWS CWI exam prep course page.

How you take it depends on your situation:

  • Corporate: a refinery contractor, LNG construction firm or fabrication yard hosts the six days at its own facility for a group, practising on its welds and gauges and, where it fits, its code and procedures.
  • Online: one person follows a study plan built on the six-day outline, with course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and messages the instructor with questions. There are no set class times.
  • One-to-one: six days of sessions between the instructor and a single candidate, online or in person at a location agreed when booking.

Atlantis writes its own practice questions to the topic list AWS publishes. Nothing in the course comes from the AWS examination, and Atlantis has no view of exam content or candidates' scores.

The Corpus Christi welding economy, asset by asset

Refineries along the ship channel

AWS's own Corpus Christi page names Valero, Citgo and Flint Hills Resources among the refiners in the area. Refinery piping is built and repaired under ASME B31.3, with welding procedures and welder tests qualified under ASME Section IX. Materials run from carbon steel to chrome-moly and stainless, so preheat, interpass temperature, post-weld heat treatment and hardness records are everyday concerns. Maintenance never stops, and turnarounds bring short bursts of intense repair welding when contractors need extra QC inspectors on short notice.

LNG on the north shore of the bay

Cheniere completed its Corpus Christi Liquefaction Stage 3 project in August 2026, taking over the last of seven new trains. The U.S. Energy Information Administration reports that this makes the terminal the second-largest LNG facility in the country, behind only Sabine Pass, and that a separate midscale project with two more trains is under construction for service in 2028. Liquefaction plants are a piping inspector's environment: stainless and other low-temperature materials, impact-tested procedures, cryogenic service and large volumes of B31.3 process piping. Construction and expansion work keeps EPC contractors hiring QC inspectors who know Section IX qualification variables inside out.

Crude and condensate export pipelines and terminals

The port describes itself as the No. 1 U.S. crude oil export gateway and the third largest in the world, and it completed the fourth and final phase of its channel improvement to a 54-foot depth in 2025. Long-haul pipelines bring crude and condensate from the Permian Basin and the Eagle Ford to export docks and storage terminals around Ingleside and the Inner Harbor. Pipeline construction and repair welding is normally specified to API 1104. Terminal tanks follow their own API standards, which are not CWI exam books, but the piping and dock work around them keeps API 1104 and B31.3 inspectors busy.

Offshore and marine fabrication in Ingleside

Kiewit fabricated and integrated the topsides for the Appomattox platform at its yard in Ingleside, a structure Kiewit describes as 35,000 tons, along with suction piles and mooring equipment. AWS points to offshore platform fabrication along the Corpus Christi Ship Channel, marine structural welding and shipbuilding as part of the local demand. Offshore structural specifications commonly call up AWS D1.1, while the process modules on a topside bring B31.3 piping into the same yard, so a yard inspector may move between two codes in a day.

Petrochemicals, wind cargo and industrial construction

Petrochemical plants in Nueces and San Patricio counties add more process piping and pressure equipment, and the port says it is the top Gulf Coast port for wind turbine imports. New industrial buildings, docks, pipe racks and support steel across Portland, Robstown, Aransas Pass and Kingsville bring structural welding under D1.1.

Who hires CWIs on the Coastal Bend, and what they look for

  • EPC contractors on LNG and petrochemical projects staff QC departments with CWIs who can track welder qualifications against joints, verify material and filler traceability, and accept welds before they move to NDT.
  • Refinery maintenance and turnaround contractors want inspectors who can start quickly and know Section IX and B31.3 well enough to keep a turnaround moving.
  • Fabrication yards need in-house inspectors for fit-up, welding and visual acceptance on structures and modules.
  • Pipeline operators and construction contractors hire API 1104 inspectors for mainline, tie-in, station and dock work.
  • Third-party inspection firms place CWIs at vendor shops and on site for owners; see third-party inspection in Corpus Christi.

Much of this work is contract-based, so a CWI who can document a long string of short jobs has an edge. For an overview of how the credential affects career options, read CWI requirements and career impact, and for regional pay comparisons, code inspector vs CWI pay on the Gulf Coast.

Picking the Part C book for Coastal Bend work

You choose your open-book code when you apply to AWS. The options are D1.1 for structural steel, API 1104 for pipelines, D1.2 for aluminum, D1.5 for bridges, D15.1 for railcars and locomotives, D17.1 for aerospace, the ASME package combining Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. Around Corpus Christi three of them do most of the work.

Where you weld or inspectBook to considerWhat Part C asks you to apply
Refinery, LNG or petrochemical piping and pressure equipmentASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3Qualification variables, impact testing, examination and acceptance rules for process piping
Export pipelines, gathering lines, terminal and dock tie-insAPI 1104Procedure and welder qualification by destructive test, and field acceptance standards
Offshore topsides, jackets, pipe racks, industrial buildingsAWS D1.1Prequalified joints, tubular connections, tolerances and visual acceptance

If you work on LNG trains, the ASME book is the obvious choice, because almost every weld you see will be qualified and examined under those documents. Yard hands who never touch piping are usually better served by D1.1. Use the edition AWS lists for the exam, which may be older than the one on site. For pipeline candidates, the API 1104 acceptance criteria guide and the API 1104 summary are useful reading; yard candidates can start with the AWS D1.1 overview.

The AWS Corpus Christi Section and the local welding pipeline

Corpus Christi has its own AWS section, part of District 18. Its posts include a welder competition run with District 18 at the Nueces County Junior Livestock Show, held at Robstown Early College High School, where young pipe and plate welders competed for AWS scholarships. For a CWI candidate the section is a place to meet inspectors and QC managers, find people who can verify your work history for the AWS application, and hear which contractors are mobilizing. Contact details are on its pages at sections.aws.org.

Del Mar College is the region's main college welding route. Its Welding Applied Technology program offers an Associate of Applied Science and several certificates, including advanced and industry welding and an apprentice pipefitter certificate, at the Windward Campus. A degree or certificate can shorten the experience AWS asks for, depending on how AWS classifies it, and a school record is easier to prove than years of informal work. Del Mar is named here as part of the local talent pipeline, not as an Atlantis partner or venue.

Booking the exam from Corpus Christi

AWS's confirmation letter, sent when it accepts your application, includes the eligibility code you give Prometric to schedule Part A and Part C. Part A is 150 questions on fundamentals; Part C is roughly 50 to 65 questions in your chosen code with the book open. Both are computer-based, and Prometric's site shows the centers closest to the Coastal Bend.

Part B is run by AWS at its own seminar and exam locations. It combines hands-on tasks with tools and specimens AWS provides and 46 questions. AWS has a CWI location page for Corpus Christi that says its classes serve Portland, Robstown, Ingleside, Aransas Pass and Kingsville, but when we checked it in November 2026 it showed no upcoming seminars in Texas. Check the AWS seminar and exam schedule early, and be prepared to drive to Houston, San Antonio or wherever the nearest session falls. You need at least 72% on each part. AWS publishes its exam fees on aws.org; to budget for travel, the code book and time off, see the CWI exam cost planner.

Studying around turnarounds, commissioning and hurricane season

Work on the Coastal Bend comes in waves. Refinery turnarounds bring weeks of twelve-hour days, LNG construction and commissioning run to tight milestones, offshore jobs mean hitches away from home, and hurricane season from June through November can shut sites and shuffle schedules with a few days' warning. The online format bends around all of that because nothing happens at a fixed time. A practical pattern is to do the fundamentals during a slack period, take your code book to work and look up the clauses that apply to the joints you see, measure every cut-out and test coupon you can get, and keep the timed practice papers for the last two weeks before your Prometric appointment.

Many local candidates come from pipe welding and know a good root pass by feel. Part B rewards a different habit: read the documents first, measure with the gauge, write the number, then compare it with the stated limit. The Practical NDT welding workshop lets you rehearse inspection steps in a browser on days off.

Corporate delivery at a Coastal Bend yard, plant or contractor

An employer preparing a group can host the six days at its own facility. An Ingleside yard might run the code day in D1.1 for its structural inspectors and in the ASME book for its piping QC staff. A turnaround contractor might want every exercise built on B31.3 and Section IX, using its own weld maps and procedure qualification records. A pipeline contractor can run the code day in API 1104 with its own welder test records.

On the practical day the group uses the company's own fillet gauges, bridge cam gauges and hi-lo gauges on real welds, including test coupons and production cut-outs. Timing can be planned around turnarounds, commissioning milestones and storm season. Each candidate still applies to AWS personally and must meet the eligibility and vision rules on their own; the employer cannot file the experience record or eye examination for them.

One-to-one preparation for a single Corpus Christi candidate

A candidate who wants the instructor's full attention can book the six days as one-to-one sessions. Online sessions suit offshore hitches and rotating shifts. In-person sessions happen at a location agreed when you book, since Atlantis keeps no premises in the city. This format works well for a Del Mar graduate who has built up experience and wants structure, or for a pipeline inspector who passed two parts and needs targeted work on the third. For a sense of where candidates tend to drop marks, see CWI results by exam part.

Eligibility and the vision record

AWS links the work experience it requires to your education. A high school diploma or equivalent means five years of welding-related work; an associate degree in an engineering technology, engineering or physical science field means two; a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology means one. AWS decides whether a particular Del Mar credential qualifies for a shorter route. You also need an AWS Visual Acuity Record showing near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without correction, and a color perception test, performed by a qualified practitioner within the period AWS allows before the exam. If you are short on experience, the Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) lets you work under a CWI while you build it. The complete table is on the national CWI exam prep page.

After the CWI: careers on the Coastal Bend

AWS keeps the CWI valid for nine years, with renewals at years three and six and recertification at nine. Locally, the next step tends to follow the asset you work on:

  • LNG and refinery inspectors often add nondestructive testing so they can run ultrasonic or magnetic particle checks themselves. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies NDT staff after training and logged hours, and Atlantis provides that training; see NDT training in Corpus Christi and ultrasonic testing in LNG. In-service inspection certifications such as API 510 and 570 are run by API under its own rules, and Atlantis does not train for them.
  • Yard and offshore inspectors deepen their structural and tubular knowledge and look toward the Senior CWI; see the Senior CWI pathway and ultrasonic testing offshore.
  • Visual inspection skills grow with VT Level 2 training; see also visual testing and weld inspection.

If you are weighing credentials, compare AWS CWI, API 577 and ASNT Level II. Local pages: ultrasonic testing in Corpus Christi, weld inspection services in Corpus Christi and the Practical NDT simulator for Corpus Christi.

Other Gulf Coast CWI pages and requesting a quote

Nearby and comparable pages: Houston, Beaumont, San Antonio, Lake Charles and Baton Rouge.

For a quote, tell us the format you want (corporate, online or one-to-one), the number of candidates, each person's schooling and welding history in outline, and the Part C book each plans to choose. For corporate delivery, add the site location, gauges and sample welds available, and the turnaround or commissioning dates to avoid. Send it through the Corpus Christi CWI enquiry form. Atlantis quotes the course on request; AWS publishes its own exam fees.

faq.q: Can I attend the CWI course at an Atlantis classroom in Corpus Christi?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Corpus Christi. You can study online at your own pace with instructor support, book one-to-one sessions online or in person at an agreed location, or have your employer host the six days at its facility. See the outline.
No. AWS administers the examination, decides eligibility and issues the certification to candidates who pass. Atlantis prepares candidates, and the course has no AWS approval or endorsement.

faq.q: Which Part C code should an LNG or refinery inspector in Corpus Christi choose?
faq.a: Usually the ASME option, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, because process and cryogenic piping at refineries and liquefaction plants is qualified and examined under those documents.

faq.q: I build offshore topsides in Ingleside. Which code fits?
faq.a: AWS D1.1 for structural work on jackets, decks and pipe racks. If your role is mainly module piping, the ASME option may suit you better. See AWS D1.1.

faq.q: Where do Corpus Christi candidates take the exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C at a Prometric center, booked with the eligibility code in your AWS confirmation letter. Part B at an AWS seminar location; AWS has a Corpus Christi page, but in November 2026 it listed no upcoming Texas seminars, so check the schedule and expect to travel.

faq.q: Is one-to-one better online or in person?
faq.a: Online suits offshore hitches and rotating shifts; in person happens at a location agreed when you book. Both give six days of one-to-one time with the instructor.

faq.q: Can a turnaround contractor have the course run at its yard before a shutdown?
faq.a: Yes. Corporate delivery brings the six days to your facility, uses your gauges, weld maps and procedure records, and can be timed around turnaround and storm-season schedules. Request a quote.

faq.q: Are the practice questions real AWS exam items?
faq.a: No. Atlantis writes every practice question and timed paper to the topic areas AWS publishes, and it has no access to the AWS examination or its question bank.

faq.q: Does a Del Mar College welding degree shorten the experience requirement?
faq.a: It may. AWS lets relevant education reduce the work experience it asks for, but AWS decides how a particular degree or certificate is classified. Check the current rules on aws.org before you apply.

faq.q: Does Atlantis offer NDT training for Corpus Christi?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training in VT, MT, PT and UT; the employer certifies its staff under its written practice. See NDT training in Corpus Christi.
